You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the orthorhombic space group Immm, space-group number 71, with Hall symbol "-I 2 2". The supplied input cell is not the conventional Immm cell: its lattice parameters are a = 6.88268143 Å, b = 6.882681430000001 Å, and c = 6.88268143 Å, with interaxial angles α = 150.12120835°, β = 146.44700263°, and γ = 45.53638811000001°. This six-atom input cell contains the declared composition Sr₂Cu₁O₃. Coordinates are fractional, and the input and standard frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the first, second, and third rows of P are (0.5, -0.49999999999999983, -0.5), (0.4999999999999999, -0.5, 0.5), and (-0.5, -0.5000000000000001, 0.5), respectively, and the origin shift s is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). Thus no translational offset is applied, but the nearly one-half integer matrix must be used exactly as given to recover the standard-frame description from the original input cell. The positional values are rounded to six digits after the decimal point, and no listed precision corrections are needed.

In the standard Immm description, the independent structure consists of four crystallographic orbits. Strontium occupies the fourfold Wyckoff orbit 4j, with coordinate relation (1/2, 0, z); its representative atom lies at (0.5, 0.0, 0.14678199999999997), so the single independent positional parameter is z = 0.14678199999999997. Copper occupies the twofold Wyckoff orbit 2d at the fixed representative position (0.5, 0.0, 0.5), equivalently (1/2, 0, 1/2), with no free coordinate. One oxygen sublattice occupies the twofold Wyckoff orbit 2a at the fixed representative position (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). A second, crystallographically distinct oxygen sublattice occupies another fourfold 4j orbit, again of the form (1/2, 0, z), with representative position (0.5, 0.0, 0.345292) and independent parameter z = 0.345292.

The body-centered orthorhombic symmetry expands these representatives to four Sr atoms, two Cu atoms, two O atoms from the 2a orbit, and four O atoms from the 4j orbit in the conventional standard cell. Geometrically, the Sr and second O sublattices share the same 4j symmetry family on the plane x = 1/2, y = 0, differing only in their independent heights along z: Sr at z = 0.14678199999999997 and O at z = 0.345292. The Cu atoms lie on the same x = 1/2, y = 0 line at the fixed height z = 1/2, while the remaining O atoms are anchored at the origin-type 2a positions. Together with the stated frame transformation, these orbits and lattice parameters fully specify the original six-atom input-cell geometry.
